subproblem.title: A Lipschitz map whose a.e. derivative is continuous has that derivative everywhere
subproblem.statement: Let n, l >= 0, f : R^n -> R^l, g : R^n -> L(R^n, R^l), c in R^n, r real and K >= 0. If f is K-Lipschitz on the open ball B^o_r(c), g is continuous on B^o_r(c), and for Lebesgue-almost every x in B^o_r(c) the map f has Frechet derivative g(x) at x, then f has Frechet derivative g(x) at every x in B^o_r(c).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (g : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)) (c : Rn n) (r : ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0), LipschitzOnWith K f (ball c r) → ContinuousOn g (ball c r) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(volume : Measure (Rn n)), x ∈ ball c r → HasFDerivAt f (g x) x) → ∀ x ∈ ball c r, HasFDerivAt f (g x) x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the analytic core of step 5 of the parent proof ('f is Lipschitz, hence absolutely continuous along segments; for a.e. y the segment y + [0,1]h meets the bad set in a null set (Fubini); f(y + h) - f(y) = integral_0^1 g(y + th)h dt; both sides are continuous in y; hence f is differentiable everywhere with derivative g'), stated for an arbitrary continuous a.e.-derivative g.

Notation. B := B^o_r(c) (open ball; if r <= 0 then B is empty and there is nothing to prove). L = L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm. L^n, L^1 are Lebesgue measures on R^n and R. Closed balls B_t(.).

0. Preliminaries. B is open and convex, f is continuous on B (Lipschitz). Let N0 := {x in B : f does not have Frechet derivative g(x) at x}; by hypothesis L^n(N0) = 0. Choose a Borel set N containing N0 with L^n(N) = 0 (exists_measurable_superset_of_null). Then f has derivative g(p) at every p in B minus N.

1. Fubini: almost every parallel segment meets N in a null set. Fix x, y in B and put h := y - x. The map Psi(w, t) := x + w + t h from R^n x R to R^n is continuous (so measurable for the product sigma-algebra), hence E := Psi^(-1)(N) is measurable. For each t in R, {w : (w, t) in E} = {w : w + (x + t h) in N} is a translate of N, so it has L^n-measure L^n(N) = 0 (translation invariance of Lebesgue measure). By Tonelli (Measure.prod_apply_symm), (L^n x L^1)(E) = integral^- L^n({w : (w, t) in E}) dt = 0. By Measure.measure_prod_null, for L^n-a.e. w: L^1({t in R : x + w + t h in N}) = 0. Call such w good.

2. FTC along a good segment. Since B is open, choose rho > 0 with B^o_rho(x) and B^o_rho(y) contained in B. Fix a good w with ||w|| < rho. For t in [0, 1] put sigma(t) := x + w + t h = (1 - t)(x + w) + t(y + w); since x + w is in B^o_rho(x), y + w is in B^o_rho(y) and B is convex, sigma(t) is in B. The set {t : sigma(t) in B} is open and contains [0, 1]. Define k(t) := g(sigma(t)) h in R^l, Gamma(t) := f(sigma(t)), Psi1(t) := integral_0^t k(tau) dtau and phi := Gamma - Psi1.
 (a) g is continuous on the open set B, hence continuous at every point of B; therefore k is continuous at every t with sigma(t) in B, in particular on [0, 1], and k is bounded on [0, 1] by some K1 (compactness).
 (b) phi is Lipschitz on [0, 1]: ||Gamma(t) - Gamma(t')|| <= K ||sigma(t) - sigma(t')|| = K ||h|| |t - t'| (both points in B), and ||Psi1(t) - Psi1(t')|| = ||integral_{t'}^t k|| <= K1 |t - t'|. Hence phi is absolutely continuous on [0, 1] (LipschitzOnWith.absolutelyContinuousOnInterval).
 (c) phi'(t) = 0 for a.e. t in [0, 1]: because w is good, for all t outside an L^1-null set, sigma(t) is not in N; take such t in the open interval (0, 1) (the endpoints form a null set). Then sigma(t) is in B minus N, so f has derivative g(sigma(t)) at sigma(t), and by the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt, sigma has derivative h) Gamma has derivative g(sigma(t)) h = k(t) at t. Also k is interval integrable on [0, t], strongly measurable near t (continuous on a neighbourhood of t) and continuous at t, so by the first fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_hasDerivAt_right) Psi1 has derivative k(t) at t. Hence phi has derivative 0 at t.
 (d) By AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval.const_of_ae_hasDerivAt_zero (valid for R^l-valued maps), phi is constant on [0, 1]; phi(1) = phi(0) gives
 f(y + w) - f(x + w) = Gamma(1) - Gamma(0) = Psi1(1) = integral_0^1 g(x + w + tau h) h dtau.

3. Removing w. The good w with ||w|| < rho form a subset of B^o_rho(0) of full measure, hence a dense subset of B^o_rho(0) (each nonempty open subset of B^o_rho(0) has positive Lebesgue measure). Choose good w_j with ||w_j|| < rho/2 and w_j -> 0. Then:
 (a) f(y + w_j) - f(x + w_j) -> f(y) - f(x), since f is continuous on B and y + w_j -> y, x + w_j -> x inside B.
 (b) Let K_rho := {(1 - tau) a + tau b : a in B_{rho/2}(x), b in B_{rho/2}(y), tau in [0, 1]}. It is compact (continuous image of a product of compact sets) and contained in B (B_{rho/2}(x) is contained in B^o_rho(x), B_{rho/2}(y) in B^o_rho(y), and B is convex). For ||w|| <= rho/2 and tau in [0, 1], x + w + tau h = (1 - tau)(x + w) + tau(y + w) is in K_rho. g is continuous on the compact set K_rho, hence bounded there by some K2 and uniformly continuous there. Therefore g(x + w_j + tau h) h -> g(x + tau h) h uniformly in tau in [0, 1] (alternatively: dominated convergence with the constant bound K2 ||h||), so integral_0^1 g(x + w_j + tau h) h dtau -> integral_0^1 g(x + tau h) h dtau.
 Passing to the limit in 2(d) (applied to w = w_j):
 (FTC) f(y) - f(x) = integral_0^1 g(x + tau (y - x)) (y - x) dtau for all x, y in B.

4. Differentiability. Fix x in B and epsilon > 0. Choose eta > 0 with B^o_eta(x) contained in B and ||g(z) - g(x)|| <= epsilon for all z in B^o_eta(x) (g is continuous at x). Let ||h|| < eta. Then x + tau h is in B^o_eta(x) for tau in [0, 1], and by (FTC) with y = x + h,
 f(x + h) - f(x) - g(x) h = integral_0^1 (g(x + tau h) - g(x)) h dtau,
 whose norm is <= epsilon ||h||. Hence ||f(x + h) - f(x) - g(x) h|| <= epsilon ||h|| for all sufficiently small h, for every epsilon > 0; that is, f(x + h) - f(x) - g(x) h = o(||h||) as h -> 0 (hasFDerivAt_iff_isLittleO_nhds_zero, Asymptotics.isLittleO_iff). So f has Frechet derivative g(x) at x, for every x in B.
proof_key_steps: Enclose the bad points in a Borel null set N
Tonelli plus translation invariance: for a.e. w the segment x + w + [0,1](y - x) meets N in an L^1-null set
On such a segment f(sigma(t)) - integral_0^t g(sigma) h is Lipschitz, hence absolutely continuous, with a.e. zero derivative, hence constant
Let w -> 0 through good w (dense), using continuity of f and uniform continuity of g on a compact convex subset: f(y) - f(x) = integral_0^1 g(x + t(y - x))(y - x) dt
Continuity of g at x gives f(x + h) - f(x) - g(x)h = o(|h|)

audit.reason: The prose and type match, including unrestricted dimensions and radius. The proof supplies a measurable null envelope, correctly applies Tonelli to translated segments, proves the segment identity using absolute continuity, and removes translations by continuity on a compact set. The final remainder estimate establishes the asserted Fréchet derivative everywhere. Empty balls and dimension zero cause no gap.
